claims.text: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) has a native alpha-plus-beta dual-phase microstructure.
Untreated TC4 has low hardness.
Untreated TC4 has suboptimal friction and wear performance under extreme-contact conditions.
LENS can produce a functionally graded transition from a TC4-like composition to a refractory HEA over a thickness of approximately 100–200 micrometers.
Substrate preheating at 300–500 °C mitigates thermal mismatch during deposition.
Post-deposition annealing at 800–900 °C for 1 hour relieves residual stresses.
A continuous compositionally graded interface minimizes abrupt thermal and compositional mismatch.
The graded interface reduces residual interfacial stresses.
The graded interface prevents formation of brittle intermetallic phases at the coating-substrate junction.
Reducing stress concentrations and thermal mismatch enhances bonding between the refractory HEA coating and TC4.
The upper refractory HEA layer will possess a stable, solid-solution-strengthened microstructure.
The solid-solution-strengthened HEA microstructure provides high surface hardness.
The solid-solution-strengthened HEA microstructure improves wear resistance.
Integrated spectroscopic and thermographic monitoring ensures that the intended composition gradient is achieved precisely.
The treated surface will have at least approximately 50% greater hardness than untreated TC4.
The treatment will significantly reduce wear rate relative to untreated TC4 under high-contact, extreme-service conditions.
The treatment will significantly reduce friction relative to untreated TC4 under high-contact, extreme-service conditions.
The coating process will preserve the toughness and overall mechanical stability of TC4.
Performance improvements depend on achieving a defect-free, continuous compositional gradient.
The magnitude of hardness and wear improvement depends on the precision of in-situ monitoring and process control.
